skill_entry.name: Redundant statement, member, branch, specifier or scope (nit)
skill_entry.trigger: Added lines in one of seven closed shapes: (a) a lambda in a std::function slot that only forwards its parameters, in order, to one free function; (b) an `} else {` whose every assignment repeats the variable's initializer above the `if`; (c) `struct X {` with `public:` first; (d) a repeated zero-argument call on one object where a local holds its result; (e) a new struct with an id or count member beside a pointer to a different type that exposes the same value; (f) `size_t n<name> = 0` beside a std::vector `<name>`; (g) a loop header replaced by a bare `{` while end-of-body resets stay; (h) a loop casting each `(T)obj[k]` where obj's element type is T.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. BASE from the PR's baseRefOid, never the live base branch. 2. Grep each shape (references/procedures.md); record file:line at HEAD. 3. (a): find the slot alias via `std::vector<ALIAS> <slot>;` and the callee declaration; compare types after namespace resolution; fire only on an exact match with no capture, conversion, reorder, drop or extra argument. 4. (b): read the whole function. 5. (d): one function body (`@@` headers); note pointer locals (`(*devs)[0]`). 6. (e): added-struct hits only; read the pointee member; grep every writer; a writer leaving the pointer null means ask. 7. (f): std::vector only. 8. (g): read the whole block. 9. (h): resolve typedefs. 10. One nit per shape per PR, at the first hit, ending 'etc'.
skill_entry.question: If this statement, member, branch, specifier or scope were deleted, would any observable state, any type, or any build change, or does the surrounding code or the language already give exactly what it gives?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A lambda that captures, converts, reorders, drops or adds an argument, or calls a member on a looked-up object (429249ead6:798-801 stayed). A count beside std::array or T[N] (3010846319 misread). A member re-read, not a call (tron-1722); a call on another object (tron-4353); repeated `getenv` (duplicate-logic check). A pointer to the enclosing type; a member added to an existing struct; a member with no reader (dead-symbol check). A cv-qualifying, widening or pointer cast. A memset with no removed loop (hot-path check). An explicit `= 0` (review body 4125818552). Redundancies outside the seven shapes (tron-1827, tron-2646 silent). Never block: approvals came 1-11 minutes after the ask; three of eight asks never applied. Withdraw after an author fact (2790097310, 2790148917).
skill_entry.finding_shape: "<'minor nit:' | 'a bit pedantic but' | nothing>: `<thing>` is redundant here... <one reason: members are public by default / `<local>` already holds it / `<ptr>->idx` already has it / already initialized to these values / you're no longer running a loop>. <optional: Would it be clearer to just do `<one-line replacement>`?> <optional: Or is there some <state> where <it is needed>?>" A one-line replacement goes in a ```suggestion block. One comment per shape per PR, anchored at the first hit in file order, ending 'etc' or 'and similarly elsewhere' when the shape repeats.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: nit only. His own words: 'minor nit:' (3391446464), 'I know this is pedantic... but' (2700506675), 'a bit pedantic but' (2976643305), 'isn't `device_idx` redundant here?' (2913598312), 'it seems like `nshards` is redundant' (3010846319), a bare ```suggestion block with no words (3029340601). The same register appears outside this check: 'kinda pedantic, but' on a default-argument echo (2789826297, tron-2011) and on constexpr placement (2947931435, tron-2176), and 'a bit pedantic' in the APPROVED review body 4125818552 (tron-2438). 'Not blocking' spelled out: 0 corpus hits; the approval arrives minutes later regardless (5 min 19 s on tron-2176, 56 s on tron-2223, 11 min 3 s on tron-2906, each at the commented commit).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, then the full enclosing function or type at HEAD (shapes b, d, g), then other files: the member declaration that names the slot alias, the alias, the callee declaration and its enclosing namespace lines (shape a); the pointee type and every writer of the id member in h/ and src/ (shape e); the typedef chain of the indexed object (shape h). Also `gh pr view N --json baseRefOid` for BASE. Not the PR body, not commits, not CI, not runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check <n>: redundant statement, member, branch, specifier or scope (nit)

Setup. BASE is the merge base against the PR base branch AS IT WAS at review time. `gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName,baseRefOid,mergeCommit`; BASE=`git -C WT merge-base HEAD <baseRefOid>`. If `git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/<baseRefName>` returns HEAD itself, the branch already contains the merged PR and that result is wrong (on PR 2176: `git merge-base 8e19ea3e62 origin/hwattention_sync` = 8e19ea3e62; baseRefOid 363edb2910 gives the 20-file, 1176-added-line diff). Save it: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD > pr-u0.diff; git -C WT diff BASE HEAD > pr.diff`. Context lines that `grep -A` prints carry an `N-` prefix (line number, dash); every second-stage filter below allows `^[0-9]+[-:]`.

1. Lambdas pushed into callback slots (shape a): `grep -nE -A1 '\.(push_back|emplace_back)\(' pr-u0.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+[-:]\+.*\[[^]]*\]\s*\('`. This catches the one-line form `x.push_back([](...) {` and the clang-format split form (`x.push_back(` on one line, `[](...) {` on the next). Do not grep `= [`: it matches helper lambdas (`auto is_special_value = [](float f) {`) and fmt strings (`[{}-{}] (count={})`). For each hit read the lambda at HEAD (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'L,L+4p'`). Keep it only if its body is one call whose argument list equals the lambda parameter list in order; a capture (`[&, i]`), a member call on a looked-up object (`get_device_dma_tracker().await_layer(l)`), a conversion, a dropped or added argument = no finding. Then find the slot's element type from its member declaration (`git -C WT grep -n -E '\b<slot>\b' HEAD -- FILE`, read `std::vector<ALIAS> <slot>;`), the alias (`git -C WT grep -n -A1 'using ALIAS' HEAD -- FILE`) and the callee (`git -C WT grep -n 'CALLEE(' HEAD -- h`). Compare types after namespace resolution: read the `namespace` lines above the callee (`git -C WT show HEAD:h/tron/gof.hpp | grep -nE '^namespace|^struct node_base|^using'`); `node_base*` declared inside `namespace tron::hardware` with `namespace tron { struct node_base; }` above it equals `tron::node_base*`. Parameter names never matter. Exact types and order = finding.
2. Else branch that repeats initializers (shape b): `grep -nE '^\+\s*\} else \{' pr-u0.diff`. Map each hit to HEAD through its `@@` header and read the whole function (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'S,Ep'`). For each `VAR = RHS;` in the else find `TYPE VAR = INIT;` above the if in the same function; finding only when every RHS equals INIT (treat `0` and `nullptr` for a pointer as equal). An else that assigns anything else, or with no assignment, is cleared.
3. Redundant first access specifier (shape c, struct form only): `grep -nE -A1 '^\+\s*struct [A-Za-z_0-9]+[^;]*\{\s*$' pr-u0.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+[-:]\+\s*public:'`. Confirm no other specifier sits between the brace and the hit. The `class X {` + `private:` mirror is not a shape (0 instances in Wade's 267 texts and 0 added `public:|private:|protected:` lines in the 15 silent diffs).
4. Repeated zero-argument accessor (shape d): list the changed functions from the hunk headers, `grep -oE '^@@.*@@.*' pr-u0.diff | sort -u`. For each function body at HEAD list locals of the form `auto\*? NAME = EXPR;` or `auto const& NAME = *EXPR;` where EXPR is a zero-argument call (`pos_list_devices()`, `obj.size()`); the finding is a later textual repeat of EXPR (same callee, same object) in the same function body. Two calls in two functions are not a finding (gof.cpp:260 on_save_impl and :385 gof_flush_partial on PR 2176). A plain member read after a local (`dev->num_fetchers` after `auto num_fetchers = dev->num_fetchers;`) is not a call. Read whether NAME is a pointer or a reference before writing the suggestion (`(*devs)[0]`, not `devs[0]`). `getenv` belongs to duplicate-logic-use-existing-helper.
5. Id or index member beside a pointer member (shape e): `grep -nE '^(@@|\+\s*struct [A-Za-z_0-9]+\s*\{|\+\s*(uint32_t|uint64_t|int|size_t) [a-z_]*(idx|index|_id)\s*(=[^;]*)?;|\+\s*[A-Za-z_:]+\* [a-z_]+ = )' pr-u0.diff`. Keep an id hit only when it sits between an added `struct NAME {` line and that struct's closing brace (a hunk whose `@@` header names a function or `public:` is a function local or an existing class: discard; on PR 2176 all five `size_t device_idx = device_index_of(dev);` hits are locals). Pointee field: `git -C WT grep -n 'struct POINTEE' HEAD -- h` then read for `idx`; a pointer to the enclosing type itself (tree links) never counts. Writers: `git -C WT grep -n '\bMEMBER\b' HEAD -- h src`; record for each writer whether it also sets the pointer. One writer that leaves the pointer null = ask the 'transient state' question, assert nothing.
6. Count beside a container (shape f): `grep -nE -A1 '^\+\s*std::(vector|array)<' pr-u0.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+[-:]\+\s*size_t n[a-z_]* = 0;'`. Read the container type: std::vector = finding; std::array<T, N> or T[N] = capacity, the count is the fill level, no finding.
7. Loop header turned into a bare block (shape g): `grep -nE -A2 '^-\s*(for|while) \(' pr.diff | grep -E '^[0-9]+-\+\s*\{\s*$'` (on PR 2223: removed `for (auto dev : *pos_list_devices()) {` at diff line 277, added `{` at 278). Open the block at HEAD from the `{` to its closing brace; list end-of-body statements that only prepare the next iteration (`memset(`, `.clear()`, `= 0;`) and the brace pair plus indentation.
8. Per-element cast of an already-typed object (shape h): `grep -nE '^\+.*\((bf16|float|uint(8|16|32|64)_t)\)\s*[a-z_]+\[[a-z_]+\]' pr-u0.diff` inside a loop; resolve the declared element type of the indexed object through its typedef chain (`git -C WT grep -n 'using OBJ_t' HEAD -- h`); finding only when it equals the cast target exactly. A cast that adds a cv-qualifier (`(volatile bf16) * (cpt + lc)`), changes width or signedness, or casts a pointer is not a redundancy.
9. Report: one comment per shape per PR, anchored at the first hit in file order, nit, question form, with the one-line replacement in a ```suggestion block when it is one line, ending 'etc' or 'and similarly elsewhere'. Withdraw after an author fact. Never block.

At HEAD h/tron/models/model.hpp:795-802 two lambdas `[](bf16** h, size_t t, size_t nk, size_t l, size_t hs, tron::node_base* n) { tron::hardware::gof_on_save_k(h, t, nk, l, hs, n); }` go into `on_save_k`/`on_save_v`, declared :629-630 as `std::vector<kv_save_observer_t>`; alias :627-628 `std::function<void(bf16**, size_t, size_t, size_t, size_t, tron::node_base*)>`; callees h/tron/gof.hpp:85-90 `gof_on_save_k(bf16** heads, size_t tok_ix, size_t n_kv_heads, size_t layer, size_t head_size, node_base* hint)`, :91 gof_on_save_v, :97 `gof_flush_partial(size_t, size_t, node_base*)` inside `namespace tron::hardware` (:21) with `namespace tron { struct node_base; }` (:17-18); on_flush_partial alias :633-634. Three forwarders match exactly -> one comment anchored at :795 with 'etc'. The :805-806 on_await_dma and on_forward_poll lambdas call a member on `get_device_dma_tracker()` -> no finding; they stayed at the fix commit 429249ead6 model.hpp:798-801 ('Simplify observer registration; document xfer_gof as temporary', which pushes gof_on_save_k, gof_on_save_v, gof_flush_partial directly at :795-797) with no comment. Steps 2-8 on PR 2176: 3 `} else {` hits in the new file h/pos/hwattention_dump.hpp, none redundant; 0 struct+public; 0 same-function accessor repeats; 5 id hits, all function locals, discarded; 0 count-beside-vector; 0 loop-to-block; 0 per-element casts.

Other verified anchors. 2913598312 (tron-2089, dbd7478b7e h/pos/gof.hpp:111-112 `uint32_t device_idx = 0;` beside `PosDevice* dev = nullptr;` inside `struct shard` :109; pointee h/pos/device.hpp:236-237 `struct PosDevice { int idx;`); final.widen_delta: New check, no existing check widened. Two amendments to SKILL.md 'How Wade words a finding'. (1) The sentence 'He does not comment on formatting, brace style, benchmark method, the C++ guide, or kernel arithmetic line by line' is contradicted by 3391446464 (redundant `public:`) and 2976643305 (leftover braces and indentation after a loop became a block); replace with: 'He does not hand-format a hunk, cite the C++ guide, or go through kernel arithmetic line by line, but he posts language-hygiene nits on a redundant keyword, a leftover scope or a repeated statement (check <n>).' (2) The severity list 'Severity is stated: "Nit:", "Fine as a first step", "Not blocking", "Coverage gap:"' includes "Not blocking", which has 0 hits in the 334 reviews, 243 inline comments, replies and 11 issue comments (facts lens count); his nit register is 'minor nit:', 'a bit pedantic but', 'kinda pedantic, but', 'I know this is pedantic'. Suggest striking "Not blocking" or marking it as unattested. Placement suggestion: a new heading 'Checks on code hygiene' after check 13, nit-only.

All eight are Wade's own words; none contains pasted assistant text (no 'Claude', 'AI' or 'assistant' marker in any member body; the PR 2233 and PR 2906 pasted texts are other comments on those PRs). Outcomes: 4 changed (2954613896, 2913598312, 2789831855, 3391446464), 3 never applied with no follow-up (3029340601 at open head 1a88e897e1, 2976643305 and 3010846319 both still at the current HEAD), 1 with no outcome (2700506675, PR 1877 closed unmerged). changes_made: Step 1 grep replaced by the two-stage push_back/emplace_back form (`grep -nE -A1 '\.(push_back|emplace_back)\(' | grep -E '^[0-9]+[-:]\+.*\[[^]]*\]\s*\('`). Three refuters proposed three different regexes; I ran all on PR 2176 (BASE 363edb2910): the draft's one-line regex found 1 of 5 slot lambdas plus 2 helper lambdas and 2 fmt strings; the executability lens's `\[..\]\s*\(..\)\s*\{` found all 5 plus 1 helper lambda; the chosen form found exactly the 5 slot lambdas and, on the 15 silent diffs, only 2 capturing lambdas. The `=` alternative is dropped.

Shape (c) narrowed to the struct+public: form; the class+private: mirror dropped (precision lens: 0 instances in Wade's texts and 0 added specifier lines in the silent diffs; facts lens did not object).

Shape (d) narrowed to a repeated call expression on the same object inside one function body; `getenv` moved to duplicate-logic-use-existing-helper; member re-reads (tron-1722) and calls on a different object (tron-4353) listed as do-not-fire; step 4 bounded by the `@@` function headers; the draft's silent drop of the item-row clause 'repeats an expression whose value a local already holds' is now explicit.

Shape (e) narrowed to a struct the diff creates, a pointee of a different type, no self-referential links; step 5 grep rewritten to allow a missing initializer and scoped to added-struct blocks (verified on PR 2089: struct shard at diff line 109, device_idx :117, dev :118; on PR 2176 all five hits are function locals and are discarded).
Shape (h) do-not-fire added for cv-qualifier, width and pointer casts (tron-1722 hwattention.hpp:74 `(volatile bf16) * (cpt + lc)`).
The shape list declared closed; tron-1827 repeated debug line and tron-2646 else-after-return listed as silent non-findings.

Overlap boundaries stated: memset on a hot path with no removed loop -> hot-path-avoidable-work; member with no reader -> dead-symbol-no-consumer-or-definition; repeated getenv -> duplicate-logic-use-existing-helper; explicit `= 0` -> type-and-initialization (4125818552 named as a review body on tron-2438).

residual_risks: Shape (h) rests on one unmerged PR (1877) whose head is not in the worktree; the declared element type of `vs` at 67b616f064 was never read, so the rule 'fire only when the element type equals the cast target exactly' is derived from the comment text and the silent-corpus counterexample, not from a code read of the originating case.

The step-1 grep assumes the slot push is spelled `.push_back(` or `.emplace_back(`; an assignment into a std::function member (`slot = [](...) {...}`) is not caught, by design, because the `=` form matched helper lambdas and fmt strings on PR 2176; no corpus instance of the assignment form exists either way.

Step 4 (shape d) has no grep; it needs a read of every changed function body listed by the `@@` headers, which is unbounded on a large PR (20 files, 1176 added lines on PR 2176). The refuters found 0 false positives but the cost scales with the diff.
The precision run covered the 15 saved silent diffs, not all 48 silent PRs.
